question: Should OpenClaw adopt this new opt-in durable core—its shared SQLite tables, `durable.*` configuration, authority-mode startup failure, and cross-owner recovery contract—as a supported core product surface?
rationale: This is a new persistent core subsystem and public configuration contract, not a narrow repair to an established behavior; source review cannot decide whether the availability, migration, and long-term ownership tradeoffs match maintainer product direction.

options.title: Approve a narrow staged durable core
options.body: Accept the owner-first boundary in principle, require rebasing and real enabled recovery proof, then review the storage and recovery slices in an explicitly approved order.

options.title: Keep recovery owner-specific
options.body: Decline the shared durable subsystem and ask for narrowly scoped fixes through the existing task, flow, subagent, and session owners.

options.title: Request a reduced proposal
options.body: Keep the RFC open and ask the author to identify one concrete cross-owner gap before accepting new configuration or shared persistence.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow staged durable core
recommendation.body: Accept the owner-first boundary in principle, require rebasing and real enabled recovery proof, then review the storage and recovery slices in an explicitly approved order.

likelyOwner.reason: mjnkao can clarify the intended boundary and stack dependencies, although an upstream owner must make the product decision.
